label: Late encoding steps and <DEL>, when the sequence starts with q/w/y/u/2/0/k/b
explanation: Active almost only before the copy phase. About 61% of activation mass is on original-phase steps t>=3 (none at t<2), and 39% is on the <DEL> step, which fires 23.5% of the time. Copy steps are essentially never active (0.1% of mass). In the original phase it fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token (95% of mass); repeated tokens are suppressed. The input tokens with the highest rates are m, x, z, s, 3, t and i. Rate and magnitude depend strongly on the first one or two original tokens. When the sequence starts with q it fires at 3.7x the base rate, and w/y/u/2 give about 2.7x. The top-activating examples nearly all start with q or w/y. The predicate is (first or second token in {q,w,y,u,2,0,k,b}) AND (the <DEL> step OR a first-occurrence m/x/z/s/3/t/i input at t>=3). It reaches dev F1 0.56 and mass recall 0.72. The rest looks like a graded dependence on the prefix, consistent with reading a distributed hidden-state direction, which these token sets only approximate.
